rationale: Both blocking findings from code-review.final are resolved and no new high-risk issue was introduced by the fix-up. CR-001: numbering is now keyed on the retrieval identity (self.SOURCE) rather than the storage key, so documents sharing a source can no longer start independent sequences; keying on the identity field can only merge sequences, never create a duplicate pair. The merge is safe for the datasources where file_path is meaningful — git_loader.py:358-363 and 380-384 and svn_loader.py:197-198 and 214-215 set source and file_path to the same value on both the text and the binary/compound paths, spot-verified directly, so code and SVN behavior is unchanged. CR-002: _chunk_counters is initialized in __init__, the hasattr lazy-init is gone, and the new entry-point test was mutation-checked — deleting the reset line in _load_and_process_documents makes it fail, which was confirmed by actually removing the line and observing the failure, not merely by reasoning. Every subclass defining __init__ calls super().__init__, so dropping the guard cannot raise AttributeError.

business_review.criterion: A multi-page PDF indexed via SharePoint returns content from pages past page 1, matching File datasource behavior.
A multi-chunk DOCX indexed via SharePoint returns content from beyond its first chunk.
A file larger than one processing batch (>20 Documents) is numbered continuously; no two of its chunks share a (source, chunk_num) pair.
business_review.notes: Upgraded from partial: CR-001's compound-file collision is fixed, so the criterion now holds for compound sources too.

business_review.criterion: A connector whose _process_chunk rebuilds metadata still produces chunks carrying chunk_num.

Carried forward: single-Document path now yields chunk_num=1 where it previously yielded none. Compatible, not identical.
